newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The race for premiership too close to call, according to a nationwide survey by The Nation newspaper. The premiership race between the Democrat Party's Chuan Leekpai and New Aspiration Party's Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will end in a photo-finish with Bangkok and the northern region playing decivive roles. (THE NATION).

The NAP holds an edge and is poised to win 127 seats in the November 17 election with a plus or minus-nine seat margin of error. The Democrats are set to win some 122 seats, with the margin of error being plus - or minus seats. (THE NATION)
Bangkok Post says that more than a quarter of all voters think there is nothing wrong with vote-buying, according to a survey by the election watchdog, Pollwatch.

The group quizzed 300,000 voters nationwide and was taken aback by its findings. Dr Sa-nguan Nitayaramong, chief of Pollwatch's analysis and planning division, said that 73.30 percent of those questioned knew it was illegal to buy votes but 26.6 percent thought there was nothing wrong about such activity. (BANGKOK POST)

- The finance ministry has wrapped up negotiations with the three government financial institutions for a long-term 8.5 billion baht soft loan for the troubled Don Muang Tollway project and expects to sign a preliminary agreement before the Nov 17 election. (THE NATION) - A finance ministry official said outgoing premier BAnhan Silpa-archa and Deputy Prime Minister Samak Samak Sundaravej have virtually "forced" acting Finance Minister Chaiyawat Wibulsawasdi to sign a letter of comfort for the subsidy loan package with Don Muang Tollway. (THE NATION)

- Thailand highly lucrative cellular duopoly is coming to an end next year with the arrival of new players and technologies which herald the end of what has been seen as a revenue gold mine fo rthe existing private concessionaires - Shinawatra Group's Advance Info Service (AIS) and Ucom Group's Total Access Corporation (TAC). (BUSINESS DAY)
